sourceEditorialReview.notes: All twenty-one union decisions were read against the catalog and source. Three red-herring contexts concern actual redirection from sincere uncorrected error or independent relational harms; the equivocation context concerns specific doctrines being answered with broad supernatural belief. The two retained argument-from-ignorance labels identify the express requirement to know that God could have no sufficient reason before admitting the comparative inference. They do not label the mere mention of possible reasons. The source distinguishes this burden condition from the earlier limited acquaintance counterconsideration, which is rejected. The retained appeal-to-authority label targets Schieber’s explicit appeal to anybody familiar with unnamed literature being well aware of a sharp specificity boundary, not his merely naming theories. His examples illustrate the asserted boundary but do not establish the claimed literature consensus. Rauser’s separate named projection-theorist discussion is rejected because it sketches an explanatory mechanism and does not settle his distinct nonentailment argument by status. The final subjective-validation label is limited to Rauser’s concluding move from finding enormous richness in his own ecumenical dialogue to being persuaded that God is actualizing relational value through the present degree of disagreement (events 1553–1567). The host’s preceding UK example is excluded. The earlier limited personal-dialogue possibility illustration receives no such label. All thirteen rejections were checked, including unsupported base-rate/scope labels and the distinction between an underdefended relational premise and begging the question. Five labels from the unsaved first draft were withdrawn after definition review. No automatic tag quota, new scores, critique changes, or controller override was used.
